I found the fault in [collection.py](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py:942). `_walk` follows internal directory symlinks and records their children. `_build_collection_tar` then passes resolved paths to `tarfile.add`, turning symlinks into regular entries. On install, `install_artifact` creates manifest directories with `mkdir` and `_extract_tar_file` writes file content without checking whether the tar member is a symlink. The tar helpers expose streams but discard the `TarInfo` needed for that check.

A fix should record each internal directory link once, preserve internal file and directory links with relative `linkname` values, copy external file targets as regular files, and validate resolved targets against the collection root before restoring links. External directory-link behavior needs a decision: [an existing test](/app/test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py:474) expects it to be skipped. Other [symlink tests](/app/test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py:492) assert the current expansion behavior.

I recorded the detailed findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). **No project source or tests were changed**: this run was constrained to fault localization. I did not run tests.

Updated [collection.py](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py) so collection tar builds preserve internal file and directory symlinks, copy external file targets as regular files, and record directory links without expanding their contents. Install now checks link targets and destination paths before restoring symlinks. The tar helpers return both `TarInfo` and a readable stream.

Updated [test_collection.py](/app/test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py) with build, install, and unsafe extraction coverage. **All 62 local collection tests pass**, and `git diff --check` is clean.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** [_extract_tar_file](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py:1401) and [_extract_tar_dir](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection.py:1434) create missing parent directories before checking whether the resolved path stays inside the collection. If `dest/escape` links outside and a tar entry needs `escape/new/file`, extraction can create `new` outside the destination before raising an error. Validate the resolved parent before `os.makedirs`, then check again before writing.

- `PYTHONPATH=lib:test python3 -m pytest -q test/units/galaxy` — 150 passed.

Fixed the extraction issue. Both `_extract_tar_file` and `_extract_tar_dir` now check that the resolved parent stays inside the collection before creating missing directories, then check again before writing. Added a regression test confirming that nested file and directory entries cannot create directories through a symlink outside the destination.

Both reviewer test commands passed: 63 collection tests and 151 galaxy tests. `git diff --check` passed. TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM: none.
